diagram_math_checks.result: V is the supplied finite-dimensional k-vector space; Lambda V is its graded exterior algebra. j1:V -> Lambda V is the inclusion as Lambda^1 V from F4/F5. sigma1:V -> F1/F0 is v -> bar(v)+F0, well-defined and linear by the canonical Clifford generator map and word-length definition. iota1:F1/F0 -> direct_sum_m Fm/F(m-1) is the direct-summand inclusion. Phi:Lambda V -> gr_F Cl is the graded algebra isomorphism proved in steps 4.1 and 5.1. The square is a diagram of underlying k-vector spaces; only Phi is asserted to be an algebra map.

Both V-to-bottom-right paths send v to bar(v)+F0 in degree one, exactly step 4.1. All arrows point from generator to exterior algebra or symbol summand, then to associated graded. No map from all Cl to F1/F0 and no algebra map Lambda V -> Cl is asserted.

Step 3.1 identifies ordered words of length <=r as a basis of Fr. Multiplicativity in step 4.1 implies Phi(e_i1 wedge ... wedge e_ir)=bar(e_i1)...bar(e_ir)+F(r-1). Step 5.1 identifies these degree-r bases. Relations in step 1.2 replace adjacent inversions or squares by a term of length two less, killed by the quotient to degree r. Step 1.1 independently shows the exterior-action leading component arises from all wedge multiplications, while any contraction lowers exterior degree. No nondegeneracy assumption is introduced.

For r=0 the unit maps to 1+F(-1) with F(-1)=0. For n=0 the generator objects are zero while degree-zero Phi is still the unit isomorphism, consistent with step 6.1. The eight original proof steps are unchanged and do not refer to this appended illustration.
